raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Parser auto-detection returns the first rule that matches, so broad rules have to come last. The `mimo` rule matches on nothing more than a template setting `enable_thinking | default(false)`, which many chat templates do. It was ordered ahead of rules that key on model specific markers, so those templates resolve to `mimo`.

On current main, a template that contains the marker and also sets that default resolves as:

| Template contains | Expected | Detected on main |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<mm:think>` | `minimax-m3` | `mimo` |
| `<minimax:tool_call>` | `minimax` | `mimo` |
| `Step-3.5` | `step3p5` | `mimo` |
| `<steptml:invoke` | `step3` | `mimo` |
| `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` | `deepseek-v4` | `mimo` |
| `<function=` and `<parameter=` | `qwen3_coder` (tool call) | `mimo` |

The last row is the one that breaks output parsing, since the tool call parser itself is wrong.

`test_specific_rules_precede_broad_fallbacks` already states that specific rules must run before broad ones, and already guards `poolside_v1` and `minicpm5` against `mimo`. This applies the same ordering to the remaining rules.

## Modifications

- Move `mimo` after the marker based rules in `REASONING_PARSER_RULES` and `TOOL_CALL_PARSER_RULES`. Its position relative to `qwen`, `deepseek_v3` and `deepseek_r1` is unchanged, since those predicates cannot match at the same time as `mimo`.
- Extend `test_specific_rules_precede_broad_fallbacks` with the missing ordering checks.
- Add two tests that run detection on templates carrying both a marker and the `enable_thinking` default.

Templates with no marker still resolve to `mimo`, so detection for MiMo itself is unchanged.

Reproduction used minimal templates built from the marker plus the `enable_thinking` default, not a full vendor template.

Tests:

```
pytest test/registered/unit/parser/test_template_manager.py
43 passed, 65 subtests passed
```

Reverting only the source change, with the new tests in place, fails 12 of them.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable. This does not change kernels or model forward code.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. This does not affect inference speed.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@JustinTong0323 you own `python/sglang/srt/parser` in CODEOWNERS, so flagging this one for you. Could you add the `run-ci` label and take a look when you get a chance? CI has not run yet, so `pr-gate` is red on the missing label rather than on anything in the diff.

The change moves two rule entries so the marker based detectors run ahead of the broad `mimo` fallback, and adds tests for the six overlap cases. @chilltongx approved it after reproducing all six at the PR base and head.

@ch-wan @ispobock could one of you add a `run-ci` label? You both have the permission and recent history in `srt/parser`, and ch-wan touched `template_detection.py` on Aug 26.

The branch is rebased, so the #21065 gate passes. CI has not run in the 10 days this has been open. JustinTong0323 owns the file in CODEOWNERS.

@hnyls2002 could you comment `/tag-and-rerun-ci` here? I rebased onto main at 8838ab28, so the #21065 gate passes.

The diff moves two `mimo` detection rules below the marker-based rules and adds tests for the six templates `mimo` was masking. chilltongx approved on Aug 22.

@hnyls2002 @JustinTong0323 you both changed `template_detection.py` this week (#39665 and #38526), so I rebased this onto main at 9d6dd7b5. `mimo` sits after the new `deepseek_v41` and `gigachat35` rules, and the ordering test covers both. `main` has `mimo` ahead of `minimax_m3` at line 551, so the masking bug is live.

Could one of you comment `/tag-and-rerun-ci`? This has been open 33 days and CI has not run once.

Reviewed and independently validated at `ba4047b14140d41b590252a39dc2af56393eb5a8`.

I loaded `template_detection.py` in isolation and exercised all six overlap cases covered by this change (MiniMax M3, MiniMax, Step 3.5, Step 3, DeepSeek V4, and Qwen3 Coder combined with `enable_thinking | default(false)`). The same harness fails all six cases at the PR base `a7ec6b97f786892a73d1edfc2e35b09c37997b6c` and passes all six at the PR head, which confirms the two ordering changes are the cause of the fix.

I also checked the remaining relative ordering: the broad `mimo` predicate stays ahead of the force-reasoning fallback, which is mutually exclusive with a detected toggle, while every marker-based predicate that can overlap now precedes it.

I could not run the repository test module end-to-end on this Windows host because collection imports the Unix-only `resource` module. The isolated test executed the actual PR module and predicates, not a reimplementation. I found no correctness issue in the patch.

@@ -910,6 +910,21 @@ def test_specific_rules_precede_broad_fallbacks(self):
         self.assertLess(tool_index["step3"], tool_index["deepseek_v3"])
         self.assertLess(tool_index["qwen3_coder"], tool_index["qwen"])
 
+        # ``mimo`` keys only on ``enable_thinking | default(false)``, an idiom
+        # many templates carry, so every marker-based rule must precede it.
+        for name in (
+            "minimax_m3",
+            "minimax",
+            "step3p5",
+            "step3",
+            "deepseek_v41",
+            "deepseek_v4",
+            "gigachat35",
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(rule=name):
+                self.assertLess(reasoning_index[name], reasoning_index["mimo"])
+        self.assertLess(tool_index["qwen3_coder"], tool_index["mimo"])
+
     def test_xml_kv_requires_both_arg_tokens(self):
         template = "Hello {{ user }}"
         force, config = detect_reasoning_pattern(template)
@@ -939,6 +954,41 @@ def test_minimax_m3_rule_precedes_m2_in_both_registries(self):
             names = [rule.name for rule in rules]
             self.assertLess(names.index("minimax_m3"), names.index("minimax"))
 
+    def test_marker_rules_survive_enable_thinking_default_false(self):
+        # A template can carry both a model-specific marker and
+        # ``enable_thinking | default(false)``. The marker must win: ``mimo``
+        # matches on the toggle alone and would otherwise mask the parser.
+        toggle = "{%- set enable_thinking = enable_thinking | default(false) -%}\n"
+        cases = (
+            ("<mm:think>{{ content }}", "minimax-m3", "minimax-m3"),
+            ("<minimax:tool_call>", "minimax", "minimax-m2"),
+            ("Step-3.5 assistant", "step3p5", "step3p5"),
+            ('<steptml:invoke name="{{ tool.name }}">', "step3", "step3"),
+            ("<｜DSML｜tool_calls>", "deepseek-v4", "deepseekv4"),
+        )
+        for body, expected_reasoning, expected_tool in cases:
+            with self.subTest(marker=body):
+                template = toggle + body
+                force, config = detect_reasoning_pattern(template)
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    detect_reasoning_parser(template, None, config, force),
+                    expected_reasoning,
+                )
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    detect_tool_call_parser(template, None, config, force),
+                    expected_tool,
+                )
+
+    def test_qwen3_coder_not_masked_by_enable_thinking_default_false(self):
+        template = (
+            "{%- set enable_thinking = enable_thinking | default(false) -%}\n"
+            "<function={{ tool.name }}><parameter={{ param.name }}>"
+        )
+        force, config = detect_reasoning_pattern(template)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            detect_tool_call_parser(template, None, config, force), "qwen3_coder"
+        )
+
     def test_minicpm5_not_misclassified_as_qwen(self):
         template = (
             "{% set enable_thinking = enable_thinking if enable_thinking is defined else true %}"
